::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Oct 18th 1890  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS University of Iowa; MsL/Y58wi
:::

My dear [Florence](people/person_1520.qmd),
In the first place my [Incurable](organizations/other_37.qmd) Vote is promised two deep so I am afraid that is of no use.

I could not answer before as I was at the [G F S](organizations/other_23.qmd) annual Conference - more over my [colleague](people/person_329.qmd) took the M S away to read. She approves of it much, and we hope to put it in among the short stories, when we can.[^1] The same may be said of [Emma](people/person_1519.qmd)’s poem, but I don’t know how to fix any time.[^2] I have more to do  than I <u>can</u> do today and it is almost Church time, so good bye

Your affectionate
C M Yonge

Can you get any [Mother’s](organizations/other_31.qmd) ladies to order this

---

[^1]: Perhaps the MS was 'Limp Ladies', *MP* (August 1891), 186-168, which was the next article signed by Wilford to appear in the magazine.
[^2]: Her correspondent’s sister Emma Wilford (b. 1832/3).  A poem ‘The Treasures of the Snow: Feast of the Purification’, signed ‘W.’ appeared in *MP* (February 1891).  (The feast of the Purification is 2 February.)
